units.text: INT. WEDDING-CAKE BAKERY - DAWN
Marble counters, copper pans, a window steamed with flour dust.
The first light turns every tier of sugared lace to pale gold.
ODETTE LAMBERT-OKONKWO hunches over a six-tier cake, a piping bag trembling in her fist.
She is thirty-four and has not slept.
She works with the stubborn precision of someone refusing to feel anything.
JULIAN VESPER enters through the back door, shaking rain from his coat.
He is tall, forty, rumpled in an expensive way.
He stops when he sees her.
He had meant to be quiet.
She does not turn.
She knows his footsteps.
CECILE LAMBERT sits on a stool by the oven, ninety years old, wrapped in a shawl.
She has watched this kitchen for sixty years.
She stirs her tea and says nothing.
Hamid, the apprentice, HAMID BAJWA (20s, apron, headphones), kneads dough at the far counter, oblivious.
Beside the cooling racks, TOBIAS REEVE (50s, groom's father, rumpled tuxedo, uninvited at this hour) rubs his eyes, a cup of coffee in each hand.
You're early.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: You're awake.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: It's a wedding. I'm always awake.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: He crosses the room.
She keeps piping.
A tiny sugar rose blooms under her hand, then another.
He watches.
His fingers hover near her shoulder, then fall away.
It's beautiful.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: It's a cake.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: It's beautiful, and I'm sorry.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: She sets the bag down.
Her hands are shaking now, openly.
Julian, not today.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: When, then?
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: Not today. This is somebody else's day.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Cecile sets her cup in its saucer.
The clink is quiet and exact.
Child, let him speak.
units.name: CECILE

units.text: Grand-mère.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Let him speak.
units.name: CECILE

units.text: Julian takes a breath.
Beside him, Tobias lowers both cups and begins to back away toward the door.
I should have come back the first week. I should have called. I should have done a hundred things.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: You should have.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: But I didn't, because I was ashamed.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: She turns at last.
Her eyes are red, her mouth a straight line.
A smear of white frosting marks her cheek like a scar.
Ashamed of what?
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: That you were better than me.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: The oven timer shrieks.
Hamid pulls his headphones down, blinks at the room, and freezes.
Nobody moves to silence the timer.
You walked out of my kitchen in the middle of service.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: I know.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: Eight years. And you come back on the morning of someone else's wedding.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: I came back because I could not stand a single day more.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: Her hand closes around the piping bag.
Frosting oozes between her fingers onto the marble.
Get out.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Odette--
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: Get out!
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: She hurls the bag.
It strikes the wall behind him, bursting in a starburst of buttercream.
Julian does not flinch.
He steps closer.
Tobias bolts for the door, spilling coffee.
Cecile rises with great effort, shawl trailing, and shuffles to the timer.
She switches it off.
Silence crashes down.
Now. Both of you. Finish the cake.
units.name: CECILE
